senses.definition: A tool used for digging; a pickaxe.
(nautical, slang) An anchor.

quotes.text: It's better to amble around, drop the "pick" for a lunchtime swim or beachcomb, then find a nice anchorage for the night.

senses.definition: A pointed hammer used for dressing millstones.
A tool for unlocking a lock without the original key; a lock pick, picklock.
A comb with long widely spaced teeth, for use with tightly curled hair.
(music) A tool used for strumming the strings of a guitar; a plectrum.
(obsolete) A pike or spike; the sharp point fixed in the center of a buckler.

quotes.text: Take down my buckler […] and grind the pick on 't.

senses.definition: A choice; ability to choose.

quotes.text: France and Russia have the pick of our stables.

senses.definition: That which would be picked or chosen first; the best.
(Australia) Pasture; feed, for animals.

quotes.text: ‘She's all African grass and Brahmans. There's not a blade of native pick left, except on the ridges.’

senses.definition: (basketball) A screen.
(lacrosse) An offensive tactic in which a player stands so as to block a defender from reaching a teammate.
(American football) An interception.
(baseball) A good defensive play by an infielder.
(baseball) A pickoff.
(printing, dated) A particle of ink or paper embedded in the hollow of a letter, filling up its face, and causing a spot on a printed sheet.

quotes.text: If it be in the smallest degree gritty, it clogs the form, and consequently produces a thick and imperfect impression; no pains should, therefore, be spared to render it perfectly smooth; it may then be made to work as clear and free from picks

senses.definition: (art, painting) That which is picked in, as with a pointed pencil, to correct an unevenness in a picture.
(weaving) The blow that drives the shuttle, used in calculating the speed of a loom (in picks per minute); hence, in describing the fineness of a fabric, a weft thread.
examples: so many picks to an inch

quotes.text: Leaving a tail 2 yd long for hemstitching, weave 3 picks of plain weave and use the tail to hemstitch in groups of 8 warp ends. Weave 3 more picks of plain weave, then begin the pattern treadling following the draft in Figure 2, beginning with the border.

senses.definition: To grasp and pull with the fingers or fingernails.
To harvest a fruit or vegetable for consumption by removing it from the plant to which it is attached; to harvest an entire plant by removing it from the ground.
examples: It's time to pick the tomatoes.

senses.definition: To pull apart or away, especially with the fingers; to pluck.
examples: She picked flowers in the meadow.
to pick feathers from a fowl

senses.definition: To take up; especially, to gather from here and there; to collect; to bring together.
To remove something from somewhere with a pointed instrument, with the fingers, or with the teeth.
examples: to pick the teeth; to pick a bone; to pick a goose; to pick a pocket

quotes.text: Did you pick Master Slender's purse?
quotes.reference: c. 1597 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Merry Wiues of Windsor”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London: […] Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene i]:

quotes.text: He picks clean teeth, and, busy as he seems / With an old tavern quill, is hungry yet.

quotes.text: He was charged with attempting to pick a pocket, and they found a silver snuff-box on him,--his own, my dear, his own, for he took snuff himself, and was very fond of it.

senses.definition: To decide upon, from a set of options; to select.
examples: I'll pick the one with the nicest name.

senses.definition: (transitive) To seek (a fight or quarrel) where the opportunity arises.
(cricket) To recognise the type of ball being bowled by a bowler by studying the position of the hand and arm as the ball is released.
examples: He didn't pick the googly, and was bowled.

senses.definition: (music) To pluck the individual strings of a musical instrument or to play such an instrument.
examples: He picked a tune on his banjo.

senses.definition: To open (a lock) with a wire, lock pick, etc.

quotes.text: The lock was of a kind that Watt could not pick. Watt could pick simple locks, but he could not pick obscure locks.

senses.definition: To eat slowly, sparingly, or by morsels; to nibble.

quotes.text: Why stand'st thou picking? Is thy palate sore?
quotes.reference: 1693, John Dryden, Third Satire of Persius:

senses.definition: To do anything fastidiously or carefully, or by attending to small things; to select something with care.
examples: I gingerly picked my way between the thorny shrubs.

senses.definition: To steal; to pilfer.

quotes.text: to keep my hands from picking and stealing

senses.definition: (dated, transitive) To peck at, as a bird with its beak; to strike at with anything pointed; to act upon with a pointed instrument; to pierce; to prick, as with a pin.
(ambitransitive) To separate or open by means of a sharp point or points.
examples: to pick matted wool, cotton, oakum, etc.

(American football, informal) To intercept a pass from the offense as a defensive player.
examples: The pass was almost picked, but the tight end was able to hold on.
